title: Federal Reserve Board announces final individual capital requirements for large banks, effective on October 1
summary: The Federal Reserve Board announced final individual capital requirements for large banks on August 29, 2025, effective October 1, 2025. The requirements are informed by stress test results and include a minimum capital requirement of 4.5% and a stress capital buffer requirement of at least 2.5%. The Board proposed a rule in April 2025 to average stress test results over two consecutive years to reduce year-over-year volatility, which if finalized would require averaging 2024 and 2025 stress test results before publishing revised stress capital buffer requirements.
key_points: Final individual capital requirements for large banks announced, effective October 1, 2025
Minimum capital requirement is 4.5% for all banks (same across institutions)
Stress capital buffer requirement is at least 2.5% (varies by firm based on stress test results)
Capital surcharge for largest/most complex banks updated in Q1 each year to account for systemic risk
Rule proposed in April 2025 to average stress test results over two consecutive years to reduce volatility
Morgan Stanley's stress capital buffer requirement is pending reconsideration; final requirement expected by September 30, 2025
Banks below their total capital requirement face automatic restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments
why_it_matters: These capital requirements affect how much loss-absorbing capacity large banks must maintain, directly impacting their ability to pay dividends, execute buybacks, and pay bonuses. The proposed two-year averaging of stress test results would reduce volatility in capital requirements, making planning more predictable for affected institutions. Vice Chair Bowman characterized this as a period of transition pending finalization of the averaging rule.
market_structure_context: The announcement establishes binding capital requirements for large banks including minimum capital ratios, stress capital buffers, and systemic risk surcharges. Banks falling below requirements face automatic restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments. The proposed two-year averaging methodology for stress test results represents a potential change to bank capital calculation methodology.
important_numbers: September 30, 2025 deadline for Morgan Stanley final requirement
